charter_node_bullets: Latent field cells in a candidate universe

dm_contaminated.source: parametric lens model with one halo per member
dm_contaminated.reason: a lens model that assigns a dark-matter clump to each cluster galaxy by construction is circular for any does-lensing-follow-light test

commute_check.note: E[f(scene)] against f(E[scene]) for the mean 3-D radius. Non-zero because sqrt is concave: collapsing the ensemble to its mean scene UNDERSTATES every mean 3-D radius.

velocity_information.note: how much the line-of-sight VELOCITY narrows the depth beyond the radial number-density prior alone

null_control.note: Newtonian gravity is linear in the source, so the shell average of the resolved field EQUALS the field of the spherically averaged source exactly. The residual is the gate's quadrature floor and nothing else.

layers.L1_imaging_members: Deep imaging + member catalogue with resolved structural parameters
layers.L2_bcg: Central galaxy, resolved separately from the members
layers.L5_xray: Hot gas: X-ray density and temperature

L1_imaging_members.what: 225 members with full Sersic fits in 7 HST bands
L1_imaging_members.raw_or_derived: RAW imaging; Sersic parameters are a MODEL FIT to the light, not a mass model -- no gravity assumption

L2_bcg.what: total fluxes in up to 17 bands; no light profile
L2_bcg.note: the HFF-DeepSpace construction MODELS AND SUBTRACTS bCG+ICL before measuring other sources, so even the total is not clean

L3_icl.what: f_ICL under 5 definitions (Montes & Trujillo 2018) plus CICLE wavelet decomposition

L4_member_ifu.what: 76 single-aperture stellar velocity dispersions from MUSE pPXF (1.5 arcsec aperture, corrected to R_e/8)
L4_member_ifu.where: arXiv:2603.26869 e-print, aa.tex Appendix C, table tab:table2744; 7 cols: ID, RA, Dec, ID_MUSE, sigma, dsigma, S/N
L4_member_ifu.note: NOT resolved maps -- one number per galaxy.  NOT at CDS: the paper's data-availability statement covers only the Appendix B structural tables, so a VizieR-only search records this layer as absent.

L6_sz.what: Bolocam 140 GHz calibrated y map, ~1.4 arcmin effective resolution, ~10-14 arcmin field; plus PSZ2 G008.94-81.22 (1.41') and ACT DR5/DR6
L6_sz.where: IRSA BOXSZ ABELL_2744.tgz; VizieR J/A%2BA/594/A27/psz2; J/ApJS/253/3/clusters
L6_sz.raw_or_derived: RAW for the y map, ACT y0/fy0 and the SZ significances; DERIVED for Y5R500 and M_SZ
L6_sz.note: Y5R500 integrates inside 5xR500 where R500 comes from an assumed GNFW template and the Y-M relation -- theory-contaminated

L7_weak_lensing.what: no public per-source shear catalogue and no public binned shear profile table
L7_weak_lensing.note: the binned profiles of Medezinski 2016, Gruen 2013 and Umetsu 2014/2016 exist only as FIGURES; what those papers tabulate is NFW masses, which presuppose a dark-matter halo
L7_weak_lensing.searched: checked HLSP, BUFFALO (announced arXiv:2602.06904 'upon acceptance', not on the HLSP), and the four published lensing analyses

L8_strong_lensing.what: identified multiple-image families with spectroscopic source redshifts
L8_strong_lensing.note: the FAMILY ASSIGNMENT is sometimes model-informed; carry that distinction

L9_time_delays.what: no multiply-imaged variable source with a measured delay
L9_time_delays.note: heavy JWST multi-epoch transient coverage exists (GLASS ERS, UNCOVER, MAGNIF, ALT, SAPPHIRES, PLATE) and has produced no measured cluster-scale delay
L9_time_delays.searched: the complete census of measured cluster-scale delays is MACS J1149 (Refsdal), PLCK G165.7+67.0 (SN H0pe), MACS J0138-2155 (Encore/Requiem) and three cluster-lensed quasars

L10_environment.what: Owers+2011 AAOmega spectroscopy to R = 15.0 arcmin = 4.1 Mpc; degree-scale photo-z only beyond that
L10_environment.where: VizieR J/ApJ/728/27/table5 (1509 rows); VizieR VII/292 (Legacy Surveys DR8 photo-z)
L10_environment.raw_or_derived: RAW redshifts; photo-z DERIVED (SED template fit, no gravity assumption)
L10_environment.note: SDSS: 0 rows within 60 arcmin.  DESI EDR and DR1: 0 rows.  Tempel+2014 filaments: 0 galaxies within 0.5 deg.  4.1 Mpc is about one virial radius -- not enough for an external tidal axis.
L10_environment.searched: SDSS DR18 SpecObj cone (control Coma 1559 rows), DESI V/161 cone, Tempel J/MNRAS/438/3465 (control Coma 352)

L2_bcg.what: total fluxes; DeMaio+2018 adds aperture luminosity and stellar mass inside r < 10/50/100 kpc
L2_bcg.note: no light profile for any HFF BCG

L4_member_ifu.what: 52 aperture sigma (Granata+2026) plus 49 independent aperture sigma (Bergamini+2019)
L4_member_ifu.note: two independent pPXF measurements of the same cluster is the only such cross-check in the sample

L5_xray.what: no published radial n_e(r) or T(r) anywhere
L5_xray.note: Bolocam SZ is what keeps this cluster in the sample
L5_xray.searched: Andrade-Santos 2017/2021 (0 hits across 4 tables / 538 rows), Donahue 2014 CLASH-X (JACO profiles exist only as figures), CLASH HLSP (optical only), Mantz WtG, CHEX-MATE; eRASS1 has it but global-only with an empty KT column from a 143 s exposure giving 144 counts inside R500

L6_sz.what: Bolocam y map; PSZ2 G221.06-44.05 at 0.80 arcmin; ACT DR5 0.23', DR6 0.19'
L6_sz.raw_or_derived: RAW y map and ACT y0; DERIVED Y5R500/M_SZ
L6_sz.note: PSZ1 does NOT contain it (nearest source 209 arcmin) while PSZ2 does -- the two Planck catalogues are complementary, not nested

L10_environment.what: CLASH-VLT VIMOS spectroscopy, 4386-4391 rows, reaching R = 17.2 arcmin = 5.5 Mpc (~2.2 r200); second independent catalogue Caminha+2017 MUSE+VIMOS, 4717 rows
L10_environment.note: the widest DEDICATED spectroscopy of any Frontier Fields target, but SDSS and DESI both return literally zero rows here

L1_imaging_members.what: q and theta from SExtractor moments only; NO R_e, NO n
L1_imaging_members.note: Granata+2026 deliberately excludes it -- a quadruple merger with no single anchoring BCG; no substitute Sersic catalogue exists
L1_imaging_members.searched: VizieR description and positional-metadata searches, arXiv searches

L4_member_ifu.what: no IFU coverage of the cluster core
L4_member_ifu.note: its spectroscopy is Keck DEIMOS + LRIS and Gemini GMOS MULTI-OBJECT SLIT (1079 redshifts, 537 members) -- slit, not integral field
L4_member_ifu.searched: enumerated the four tables in J/A%2BA/709/A254 (a2744, as1063, m0416, m1149 only); searched the MUSE cluster-core literature

L6_sz.what: Bolocam y map; PSZ2 G180.25+21.03 at 1.16 arcmin
L6_sz.note: OUT OF THE ACT FOOTPRINT (Dec +37.76 against a measured ACT DR6 maximum of +20.796) and absent from SPT -- Bolocam is the only resolved SZ product for this cluster

L10_environment.what: DESI DR1 gives 2392 redshifts within 0.5 deg, 84 of them in the cluster redshift slice; SDSS has 233 within 60 arcmin and ZERO in the slice
L10_environment.where: VizieR V/161 (DESI DR1 zcat, 28,425,963 rows); SDSS DR18 SpecObj
L10_environment.note: FOOTPRINT PRESENCE IS NOT COVERAGE: the SDSS main sample is far too shallow at z=0.545, so all 233 SDSS spectra are foreground.  A raw row count would have scored this cluster as covered.

L6_sz.what: Bolocam y map; PSZ2 G228.16+75.20 at 0.53 arcmin
L6_sz.note: out of the ACT footprint (Dec +22.40 > +20.796) and absent from SPT

L8_strong_lensing.what: image families including the SN Refsdal host

L9_time_delays.what: SN Refsdal: four measured delays. SX-S1 = 376.02 d (68% interval +5.6/-5.5); S2-S1 = 9.69 d; S3-S1 = 7.92 d; S4-S1 = 19.44 d.  Combined across four independent light-curve algorithms (Polyn., GPR, SNTD, PyCS).
L9_time_delays.where: Kelly+2023 ApJ 948 93, arXiv:2305.06377 e-print, ms.tex table tab:measurementsdelaycorr
L9_time_delays.note: NOT on VizieR and NOT machine-readable: every cell of the published table is a \def macro resolved elsewhere in ms.tex, so extracting the table alone returns no numerals

L10_environment.what: SDSS 1168 redshifts within 60 arcmin, 150 in the cluster slice (= 23 Mpc reach); DESI DR1 adds 508 within 0.5 deg, 22 in slice
L10_environment.note: marginal: 150 in-slice tracers over 23 Mpc is sparse for a filament or tidal-axis reconstruction

L6_sz.what: Bolocam y map; PSZ2 G349.46-59.95; ACT DR6 at 0.29 arcmin, SNR 83.4; SPT SZ J2248-4431
L6_sz.raw_or_derived: RAW y map and ACT/SPT y0
L6_sz.note: the best-covered SZ target: Bolocam + ACT + SPT + Planck

L10_environment.what: CLASH-VLT 25x25 arcmin (Mercurio+2021), ~3850 redshifts, R ~ 17.7 arcmin = 5.2 Mpc
L10_environment.where: CLASH-VLT project site -- NOT served by VizieR
L10_environment.note: SDSS 0 rows, DESI 0 rows, Tempel filaments 0 galaxies.  Pan-STARRS also absent (Dec -44.5).
L10_environment.searched: J/A%2BA/656/A147 returns a clean 'Table or Catalog not found' on the CfA mirror; a METAcat title search for *CLASH-VLT* returns exactly one hit, J/ApJS/224/33, which is MACS J0416

L1_imaging_members.what: 870 members with q and theta from SExtractor moments only; NO R_e, NO n
L1_imaging_members.note: the ONLY target with a raw shear catalogue is also one of the two without resolved Sersic parameters

L4_member_ifu.what: MUSE mosaic covering > 14 arcmin^2 exists, but no published stellar-kinematics catalogue
L4_member_ifu.note: the raw IFU data exist; the derived kinematics do not

L6_sz.what: Bolocam y map; PSZ2 G172.98-53.55; ACT DR6 0.13'
L6_sz.raw_or_derived: RAW y map and ACT y0

L7_weak_lensing.note: THE ONLY public raw cluster shear catalogue among the seven

L10_environment.where: SDSS DR18 SpecObj; VizieR V/161; VII/292 photo-z; II/371 DES DR2; II/349 Pan-STARRS DR1
L10_environment.raw_or_derived: RAW redshifts and photometry; photo-z DERIVED (SED fit)
L10_environment.note: the second-best environment case after A2029, and the only target that combines a raw shear catalogue with usable wide spectroscopy

The Sohn+2019b MEMBERSHIP column is DERIVED (caustic/phase-space assignment presumes a dynamical mass model) and the Tempel filament field is DERIVED (a Bisous marked point process on the redshift-space galaxy field).  Use the redshifts, not the labels.
dm_contaminated.note: four independent, mutually checkable environment layers -- the only target where an external tidal axis can actually be reconstructed

acquisition_notes.method: VizieR ASU (TAP returns 403). Every pull asserted the row count AND the column list, passed -out.all=1 explicitly, percent-encoded '+' as %2B, and checked both fuzzy-fallback detectors (#Name echo, CatalogsExamined). No cone-search null was trusted; all coordinate matching was done numerically against fully downloaded tables with a positive control.
new_traps_found: The VizieR fuzzy-fallback trap is MIRROR-DEPENDENT. The same bad ID J/A%2BA/621/A41 serves 5.9 MB of an unrelated real catalogue at HTTP 200 from CDS but returns a clean 'Error=Table or Catalog not found' from vizier.cfa.harvard.edu. CfA is not merely faster, it is more truthful on bad IDs -- use it for existence tests.

A SILENT ALIASED CATALOGUE that the CatalogsExamined detector cannot see: -source=J/A%2BA/590/A30 returns #Name: J/A+A/590/A31, a DIFFERENT PAPER, with CatalogsExamined=0 and no error. The #Name echo is the only detector that catches it.
#Name: echoes the PARENT for a subtable request (J/A%2BA/594/A27/psz2 -> #Name: J/A+A/594/A27), so the echo test must be a PREFIX test; exact string equality false-positives.

NOIRLab Data Lab TAP returns errors as HTTP 200 VOTABLE. A wrong column name (target_ra; the real one is mean_fiber_ra) produced <INFO name='QUERY_STATUS' value='ERROR'> inside a normal 200 and a line-based parse rendered it as an empty count for every cluster INCLUDING the positive control. Grep for QUERY_STATUS ERROR first.

A subtable that looks like the main catalogue can hold a handful of rows: J/ApJS/247/25/table10 has 18 rows while the real SPT-ECS catalogue is /cand with 470. Enumerate subtables via METAtab before querying, and note that METAtab's `records` column sits after a free-text comment column so it must be requested explicitly.

A cone search on a table with no sky columns returns 0 rows for EVERY position including the positive control: Tempel+2014 table2 carries only Cartesian x,y,z. Without a control this reads as 'no filaments anywhere in the sky'.

Sexagesimal coordinate columns coerce silently: three catalogues serve RAJ2000 as 'h:m:s' strings, and a naive numeric cast gave RA=0.0000, Dec=-30.0000 and a fabricated 187 arcmin survey extent -- a plausible wrong number, not a crash.

FOOTPRINT PRESENCE IS NOT COVERAGE. MACS J0717 has 233 SDSS spectra within 60 arcmin and ZERO at the cluster redshift; the SDSS main sample is far too shallow at z=0.545. A row count alone scores it as covered.

A published data-availability statement can be narrower than the paper. Granata+2026 deposits only its Appendix B structural tables at CDS; the 213 velocity dispersions are Appendix C and exist only in the arXiv LaTeX source. A VizieR-only inventory records this layer as absent.
Time-delay tables can contain no numerals at all: every cell of Kelly+2023's delay table is a \def macro resolved elsewhere in the manuscript source.
acquisition_notes.sealed: KiDS and the wide binaries were not loaded, looked at, or queried at any point in this lane.

status_vocabulary.RAW_ARXIV_LATEX_ONLY: raw, but only inside a paper's LaTeX source -- invisible to a catalogue search
status_vocabulary.RAW_PIXELS_ONLY: raw, but no tabulated product exists
status_vocabulary.DERIVED_UNDER_THEORY: presupposes a gravity or mass model
status_vocabulary.PARTIAL: exists but materially weaker than the charter asks
status_vocabulary.ABSENT: confirmed absent; `searched` records what was tried

quantities.name: G
quantities.definition: Newton's gravitational constant.
quantities.source: laboratory
quantities.measurability_note: a GLOBAL constant; an object-specific value would violate charter criterion 3

quantities.name: M_enc
quantities.definition: Baryonic mass enclosed inside a stated radius of the declared centre, summed over resolved components.
quantities.source: integral of the resolved source scene
quantities.completeness: above the completeness threshold plus a statistical unresolved population
quantities.measurability_note: yes for BARYONS. A dynamical or lensing 'enclosed mass' is a different object and is NOT this one.

quantities.name: P_e
quantities.definition: Electron thermal pressure, n_e k T.
quantities.source: n_e times T_x, or SZ y deprojection
quantities.measurability_note: measurable two independent ways (X-ray n_e*T and SZ y), which is what makes it useful

quantities.name: R500
quantities.definition: Radius enclosing 500 times the critical density. RETAINED WITH A WARNING: it is defined through a mass, so any statistic binned in r/R500 that also involves mass shares a denominator with its own axis.
quantities.source: DERIVED from a hydrostatic or lensing mass
quantities.uncertainty: inherits the mass estimator's error and its equilibrium assumption
quantities.measurability_note: NOT a raw observable. Flagged by this programme's R500 tautology audit (Run AT).

quantities.name: T_x
quantities.definition: X-ray spectroscopic gas temperature.
quantities.source: spectral fit to the X-ray continuum and line ratios
quantities.uncertainty: counts-limited; unusable below ~150 counts in R500
quantities.selection: requires enough counts for a spectral fit
quantities.measurability_note: yes -- a spectroscopic measurement, theory-independent
quantities.notes: spectroscopic-like weighting is nonlinear in T, so a temperature read off an averaged spectrum is NOT the average temperature

quantities.name: a0
quantities.definition: Candidate universal acceleration scale.
quantities.source: fitted globally, once
quantities.measurability_note: a GLOBAL constant; an object-specific value would violate charter criterion 3

quantities.name: alignment_angle
quantities.definition: Angle between two declared axes (e.g. a galaxy's angular-momentum axis and the local filament axis).
quantities.source: from two independently measured axes
quantities.measurability_note: yes IF both axes come from different data; an angle between an axis and itself is not a variable
quantities.notes: parity: cos(angle) is EVEN; a SIGNED angle would be ODD and would need a handedness convention

quantities.name: axis_ratio_q
quantities.definition: Projected minor-to-major axis ratio of the light.
quantities.source: second moments or a Sersic fit
quantities.measurability_note: available for all seven target clusters

quantities.name: c_light
quantities.definition: Speed of light in vacuum.
quantities.source: laboratory
quantities.measurability_note: a GLOBAL constant; an object-specific value would violate charter criterion 3

quantities.name: distance
quantities.definition: Angular-diameter distance to the system.
quantities.source: measurement model
quantities.measurability_note: must be MARGINALISED, never promoted to a gravity variable without evidence

quantities.name: e1
quantities.definition: First component of the measured background-source ellipticity, in the declared sky frame.
quantities.source: MEASURED: a shape estimator on calibrated pixels
quantities.uncertainty: shape noise ~0.25-0.30 per component, plus a multiplicative shear calibration
quantities.selection: size and S/N cuts; the selection is itself a shear-dependent bias
quantities.measurability_note: THE raw lensing observable. A convergence map is not: it is this, plus an inversion that assumes a gravity law.

quantities.name: e2
quantities.definition: Second component of the measured background-source ellipticity, in the declared sky frame.
quantities.source: MEASURED: a shape estimator on calibrated pixels
quantities.uncertainty: shape noise ~0.25-0.30 per component, plus a multiplicative shear calibration
quantities.selection: size and S/N cuts; the selection is itself a shear-dependent bias
quantities.measurability_note: THE raw lensing observable. A convergence map is not: it is this, plus an inversion that assumes a gravity law.

quantities.name: ext_axis
quantities.definition: Unit vector of the externally imposed preferred axis (cluster-centre direction, filament axis, or principal tidal eigenvector), whichever the candidate declares.
quantities.source: from the environment reconstruction, INDEPENDENTLY of the probe whose response is being tested
quantities.uncertainty: depends on the environment catalogue depth
quantities.completeness: requires a surrounding-structure catalogue, which is the layer most often missing
quantities.selection: survey footprint around the line of sight
quantities.measurability_note: THIS IS THE GATE-1 CRUX. A constant response tensor is a coordinate stretch UNLESS its axis is fixed by an independently measured direction misaligned with the probe's radial direction.

quantities.name: field_memory
quantities.definition: Accumulated exposure of a region to a declared environmental state, with a declared decay time.
quantities.source: history integral generated by a candidate universe
quantities.measurability_note: a memory law must predict how the effect DECAYS; 'history matters' is not a law

quantities.name: g_N
quantities.definition: Magnitude of the Newtonian acceleration generated by the RESOLVED BARYONIC scene at the evaluation point.
quantities.source: solved from the resolved baryonic source scene
quantities.uncertainty: inherits the baryon budget and the scene ensemble
exact_identities: g_N = G M_enc / r_3d^2  (spherical case only)
quantities.measurability_note: constructed, not observed. In the SPHERICAL case it is an exact function of (M_enc, r_3d), so a law reading all three has two directions, not three -- this is the collapse the rank test finds.

quantities.name: g_total
quantities.definition: Magnitude of the total gravitational acceleration predicted by the candidate law on this scene.
quantities.source: candidate law applied to the scene
quantities.measurability_note: a prediction

quantities.name: g_vec
quantities.definition: Gravitational acceleration vector at a point.
quantities.source: candidate law applied to the scene
quantities.measurability_note: a prediction; only its EFFECT on tracers and photons is observable

quantities.name: graph_degree
quantities.definition: Weighted degree of a well in the source network, at a declared linking length.
quantities.source: constructed from the member catalogue and a linking rule
quantities.measurability_note: changes discretely under a merge or split, so it must be shown convergent before use

quantities.name: image_position
quantities.definition: Sky position of one image in a multiply-imaged family.
quantities.source: MEASURED: image astrometry
quantities.selection: requires a spectroscopic or colour-based family identification, which is itself model-informed
quantities.measurability_note: the positions are raw; the FAMILY ASSIGNMENT sometimes is not, and that distinction must be carried

quantities.name: kappa
quantities.definition: Convergence. A DERIVED product: the shape catalogue inverted under an assumed relation between shear and surface density.
quantities.source: DERIVED UNDER A THEORY from e1, e2
quantities.measurability_note: NOT a raw observation. Charter: do not score 'a precomputed convergence map ... as though it were the primitive observation.'
quantities.notes: DM-PRESUPPOSING when the lens model assigns a halo to each cluster galaxy by construction (e.g. the CATS Frontier Fields maps), which makes it circular for any does-lensing-follow-light test

quantities.name: m_bh
quantities.definition: Central black-hole mass.
quantities.source: M-sigma or a resolved kinematic measurement
quantities.completeness: above the catalogue limit; an unresolved population is carried statistically
quantities.measurability_note: component-specific

quantities.name: m_gas_hot
quantities.definition: Hot ionised intracluster gas mass.
quantities.source: X-ray surface brightness deprojection
quantities.completeness: above the catalogue limit; an unresolved population is carried statistically
quantities.measurability_note: component-specific

quantities.name: m_h2
quantities.definition: Molecular gas mass from a CO line and a conversion factor.
quantities.source: CO flux and alpha_CO
quantities.completeness: above the catalogue limit; an unresolved population is carried statistically
quantities.measurability_note: component-specific

quantities.name: m_hi
quantities.definition: Atomic hydrogen mass from the 21 cm line flux.
quantities.source: 21 cm integrated flux and a distance
quantities.completeness: above the catalogue limit; an unresolved population is carried statistically
quantities.measurability_note: component-specific

quantities.name: m_icl
quantities.definition: Diffuse intracluster stellar mass.
quantities.source: deep surface photometry below a stated surface-brightness cut
quantities.completeness: above the catalogue limit; an unresolved population is carried statistically
quantities.measurability_note: component-specific

quantities.name: m_star
quantities.definition: Stellar mass from a population-synthesis fit to multi-band photometry at a declared IMF.
quantities.source: photometry + stellar population model
quantities.uncertainty: 0.06 dex global M/L offset with 0.045 dex galaxy-to-galaxy scatter (mid-IR route)
quantities.completeness: above the catalogue limit; an unresolved population is carried statistically
quantities.measurability_note: yes -- but only up to one GLOBAL nuisance (Upsilon* = 0.5 to 0.06 dex)

quantities.name: mass
quantities.definition: Total gravitating rest mass assigned to the node.
quantities.source: sum of the component masses below
quantities.completeness: above the catalogue limit; an unresolved population is carried statistically
quantities.measurability_note: component-specific

quantities.name: n_e
quantities.definition: Electron number density of the hot gas at a point.
quantities.source: X-ray surface-brightness deprojection with an emissivity model
quantities.uncertainty: clumping-corrected; the correction is model dependent
quantities.selection: surface-brightness limited; stops at 0.7-1.1 R500 for the Frontier Fields targets
quantities.measurability_note: yes, and it does NOT presuppose dark matter -- emissivity depends on n_e^2 and T, not on mass

quantities.name: n_wells
quantities.definition: Number of distinct gravitational wells above a declared mass threshold within a declared radius.
quantities.source: counted off the member catalogue
quantities.measurability_note: NOT independently measurable: its value changes when a deblender splits one galaxy into two. A law reading it must converge under merge/split.

quantities.name: p_member
quantities.definition: Probability the galaxy is a cluster member.
quantities.source: measurement model
quantities.measurability_note: must be MARGINALISED, never promoted to a gravity variable without evidence

quantities.name: path_density
quantities.definition: Baryonic mass density integrated along a source-observer light path.
quantities.source: integral of the scene density along the ray
quantities.uncertainty: dominated by line-of-sight structure outside the cluster, which is usually uncatalogued
quantities.completeness: the foreground/background catalogue is the limiting layer
quantities.measurability_note: requires a line-of-sight structure catalogue that mostly does not exist at the needed depth

quantities.name: path_void_fraction
quantities.definition: Fraction of the path length spent below a declared density threshold.
quantities.source: from the path density profile and a threshold
quantities.measurability_note: as path_density

quantities.name: phi_depth_r500
quantities.definition: Baryonic potential difference between the evaluation point and a boundary. Boundary rule: zero at the fixed overdensity boundary R500 of the system.
quantities.source: solved from the resolved baryonic scene, differenced against the named boundary
quantities.uncertainty: 0.87 dex spread across the four defensible global rules in this family (Run AH), against a 0.9 dex gate margin -- the rule choice is NOT negligible
quantities.gauge: zero at the fixed overdensity boundary R500 of the system
quantities.selection: the volume rule additionally inherits the survey footprint, which is why it is the weakest of the four
quantities.measurability_note: a constructed quantity; the point of the family is that a candidate whose VERDICT changes across the four rules is flagged

quantities.name: phi_depth_saddle
quantities.definition: Baryonic potential difference between the evaluation point and a boundary. Boundary rule: zero at the nearest gravitational saddle of the baryonic potential (a physically located surface, no free constant).
quantities.source: solved from the resolved baryonic scene, differenced against the named boundary
quantities.uncertainty: 0.87 dex spread across the four defensible global rules in this family (Run AH), against a 0.9 dex gate margin -- the rule choice is NOT negligible
quantities.gauge: zero at the nearest gravitational saddle of the baryonic potential (a physically located surface, no free constant)
quantities.selection: the volume rule additionally inherits the survey footprint, which is why it is the weakest of the four
quantities.measurability_note: a constructed quantity; the point of the family is that a candidate whose VERDICT changes across the four rules is flagged

quantities.name: phi_depth_scaleradius
quantities.definition: Baryonic potential difference between the evaluation point and a boundary. Boundary rule: zero at a fixed multiple (10x) of the baryonic scale radius.
quantities.source: solved from the resolved baryonic scene, differenced against the named boundary
quantities.uncertainty: 0.87 dex spread across the four defensible global rules in this family (Run AH), against a 0.9 dex gate margin -- the rule choice is NOT negligible
quantities.gauge: zero at a fixed multiple (10x) of the baryonic scale radius
quantities.selection: the volume rule additionally inherits the survey footprint, which is why it is the weakest of the four
quantities.measurability_note: a constructed quantity; the point of the family is that a candidate whose VERDICT changes across the four rules is flagged

quantities.name: phi_depth_volume
quantities.definition: Baryonic potential difference between the evaluation point and a boundary. Boundary rule: zero at the edge of the reconstructed environmental volume (survey-footprint dependent).
quantities.source: solved from the resolved baryonic scene, differenced against the named boundary
quantities.uncertainty: 0.87 dex spread across the four defensible global rules in this family (Run AH), against a 0.9 dex gate margin -- the rule choice is NOT negligible
quantities.gauge: zero at the edge of the reconstructed environmental volume (survey-footprint dependent)
quantities.selection: the volume rule additionally inherits the survey footprint, which is why it is the weakest of the four
quantities.measurability_note: a constructed quantity; the point of the family is that a candidate whose VERDICT changes across the four rules is flagged

quantities.name: phi_lensing
quantities.definition: Lensing potential: the combination of metric potentials that deflects a null geodesic, differenced against the same boundary rule as the matter potential.
quantities.source: generated by a candidate universe from its sources
quantities.gauge: same boundary rule as the paired matter potential -- the DIFFERENCE of the two is only meaningful if both use one rule
quantities.measurability_note: only its effect on photons is observed

quantities.name: phi_slip
quantities.definition: Difference between the matter and lensing potentials at the same point under one common boundary rule. Zero iff matter and light see the same geometry.
quantities.source: difference of two candidate-generated potentials
quantities.gauge: the common rule cancels in the difference, which is what makes this quantity gauge-safe where each term alone is not
quantities.measurability_note: constructed. It is the charter's 'Do matter and light see the same geometry?' made into a number.

quantities.name: position_angle
quantities.definition: Position angle of the light's major axis, east of north.
quantities.source: second moments or a Sersic fit
quantities.measurability_note: yes, but it is a SKY-FRAME angle: an alignment statistic built from it must state its frame

quantities.name: psf_fwhm
quantities.definition: Point-spread-function full width at half maximum, as a physical length at the source.
quantities.source: measurement model
quantities.measurability_note: must be MARGINALISED, never promoted to a gravity variable without evidence

quantities.name: r_3d
quantities.definition: True three-dimensional separation from the cluster centre.
quantities.source: LATENT: sqrt(r_proj^2 + z^2) with z sampled, not measured
quantities.uncertainty: inherits the whole line-of-sight depth posterior
quantities.measurability_note: no external galaxy cluster has a measured member depth; this is the ensemble's job

quantities.name: r_e
quantities.definition: Half-light radius from a Sersic fit.
quantities.source: Sersic fit to a calibrated image
quantities.completeness: only where a resolved fit exists
quantities.selection: HST-resolved members only; absent for A370 and MACS J0717
quantities.measurability_note: yes where fitted; MISSING for 2 of 7 target clusters, which is a real inventory hole

quantities.name: r_proj
quantities.definition: Projected separation from the declared cluster centre on the sky.
quantities.source: measured: angular separation times an angular-diameter distance
quantities.uncertainty: centroid plus centre definition; the centre choice dominates (BCG vs X-ray peak vs light centroid)
quantities.measurability_note: yes, once a centre convention is declared

quantities.name: rho_env
quantities.definition: Baryonic mass density smoothed over a declared scale, around the evaluation point.
quantities.source: environment catalogue convolved with a declared kernel
quantities.uncertainty: dominated by catalogue completeness, not by shot noise
quantities.completeness: the binding constraint: a magnitude-limited environment catalogue undercounts with distance
quantities.measurability_note: yes where a surrounding-structure catalogue exists at the required radius

quantities.name: rho_star
quantities.definition: Stellar mass volume density at a point, from a deprojected light profile times a mass-to-light ratio.
quantities.source: deprojected surface photometry
quantities.uncertainty: deprojection is not unique for a triaxial source
quantities.measurability_note: up to the global M/L and the deprojection

quantities.name: sersic_n
quantities.definition: Sersic index of the light profile.
quantities.source: Sersic fit to a calibrated image
quantities.uncertainty: degenerate with sky subtraction at large n
quantities.measurability_note: yes where fitted

quantities.name: shear_m
quantities.definition: Multiplicative shear calibration bias.
quantities.source: measurement model
quantities.measurability_note: must be MARGINALISED, never promoted to a gravity variable without evidence

quantities.name: sigma_star
quantities.definition: Aperture stellar velocity dispersion of a member galaxy from a pPXF fit, inside a stated aperture.
quantities.source: pPXF fit to an integral-field spectrum
quantities.selection: IFU coverage and S/N; ~213 members across four Frontier Fields clusters
quantities.measurability_note: yes, and it is a MEASURED alternative to an assumed sigma-luminosity scaling
quantities.notes: an APERTURE quantity, not a resolved map: it is already an average, so it must pass the commutation gate before being used to stand in for resolved internal kinematics

quantities.name: sigma_turb
quantities.definition: One-dimensional turbulent velocity of the hot gas.
quantities.source: X-ray line broadening (microcalorimeter) or a surface-brightness fluctuation argument
quantities.uncertainty: large; measured directly for very few clusters
quantities.measurability_note: not available for the Frontier Fields targets

quantities.name: smoothing_scale
quantities.definition: Declared Gaussian smoothing scale at which a field-type quantity is evaluated. A PHYSICAL candidate variable, not only a technical choice (charter section 1).
quantities.source: declared by the analysis
quantities.measurability_note: it is a declaration, so it is exactly known; the question is whether the RESULT depends on it

quantities.name: t
quantities.definition: Epoch to which the node's state refers, as proper time in the cluster frame.
quantities.source: derived from redshift and an assumed distance-redshift law
quantities.gauge: zero at the observed cluster epoch (t=0 at the lookback time of the cluster redshift); differences only
quantities.measurability_note: requires a distance-redshift relation, which is one of the things under test

quantities.name: t_since_merger
quantities.definition: Time since the last major merger, from shock-front geometry and gas-star offsets.
quantities.source: inferred from merger diagnostics
quantities.selection: requires a shock or an offset to be detected
quantities.measurability_note: crudely; the gas-star offset is a direct observable but the conversion to a time is not

quantities.name: tidal_anisotropy
quantities.definition: Traceless part of the tidal tensor, normalised by its own Frobenius norm; a pure shape, gauge-free.
quantities.source: from tidal_tensor
quantities.measurability_note: constructed

quantities.name: tidal_tensor
quantities.definition: Hessian of the baryonic potential, d2Phi/dx_i dx_j.
quantities.source: second derivative of the solved baryonic potential
quantities.measurability_note: constructed. Its TRACE is fixed by the local density (Poisson), so trace and density are not two independent variables.
quantities.notes: GATE 3 hazard: sourcing this from the CATALOGUE ROW LIST rather than from the smooth density is the named repair in Run AB and changes the verdict

quantities.name: time_delay
quantities.definition: Measured arrival-time difference between two images of the same source.
quantities.source: MEASURED: light-curve cross-correlation
quantities.uncertainty: from the light-curve sampling and microlensing
quantities.completeness: essentially nil: cluster-scale time delays exist for a handful of events in the whole sky
quantities.selection: requires a variable source behind a cluster
quantities.measurability_note: raw and theory-free, and it is the single strongest matter-light consistency constraint. The problem is that almost none exist.

quantities.name: upsilon_star
quantities.definition: Stellar mass-to-light ratio in the declared band, as a GLOBAL nuisance.
quantities.source: measurement model
quantities.uncertainty: 0.06 dex, GLOBAL (0.045 dex galaxy-to-galaxy scatter, so it is one nuisance not N)
quantities.measurability_note: must be MARGINALISED, never promoted to a gravity variable without evidence

quantities.name: v_circ
quantities.definition: Circular speed implied by the gravitational field at a radius, for a tracer on a circular orbit.
quantities.source: derived from a candidate law
quantities.uncertainty: inherits the law and the scene
quantities.measurability_note: a PREDICTION, not an observation

quantities.name: v_los
quantities.definition: Line-of-sight velocity relative to the cluster systemic redshift, from a spectroscopic line centroid.
quantities.source: measured: spectroscopic redshift minus the systemic value
quantities.uncertainty: typically 20-150 km/s depending on the instrument
quantities.selection: spectroscopic targeting -- NOT the same selection as the photometric member catalogue
quantities.measurability_note: yes -- one of the cleanest direct observables in the whole scene

quantities.name: v_x
quantities.definition: x-component of the node's velocity in the cluster rest frame.
quantities.source: LATENT: transverse velocity is not measured at cluster distances
quantities.measurability_note: no: proper motions at z~0.3 are far below any current astrometric capability

quantities.name: v_y
quantities.definition: y-component of the node's velocity in the cluster rest frame.
quantities.source: LATENT: transverse velocity is not measured at cluster distances
quantities.measurability_note: no: proper motions at z~0.3 are far below any current astrometric capability

quantities.name: v_z
quantities.definition: z-component of the node's velocity in the cluster rest frame.
quantities.source: measured (= v_los)
quantities.measurability_note: yes

quantities.name: vacuum_axis
quantities.definition: Unit vector of a latent preferred-direction field.
quantities.source: generated by a candidate universe
quantities.measurability_note: if it is dynamically generated by the local source it is degenerate with source shape; only an EXTERNALLY generated axis is identifiable (GATE 1)

quantities.name: vacuum_order
quantities.definition: Scalar order parameter of a polarisable vacuum, normalised so that 0 is the unmodified vacuum.
quantities.source: generated by a candidate universe
quantities.measurability_note: NOT fittable independently at every location -- the candidate universe must specify what generates it and how it evolves

quantities.name: x
quantities.definition: Cartesian x-coordinate of the node in the cluster rest frame, origin at the declared centre. from the astrometric image centroid.
quantities.source: measured: astrometric centroid on a calibrated frame
quantities.uncertainty: 0.10 arcsec centroid -> 0.15-0.64 kpc depending on cluster redshift
quantities.completeness: members above the catalogue magnitude limit
quantities.measurability_note: two independent astrometric solutions agree to 0.026 arcsec

quantities.name: y
quantities.definition: Cartesian y-coordinate of the node in the cluster rest frame, origin at the declared centre. from the astrometric image centroid.
quantities.source: measured: astrometric centroid on a calibrated frame
quantities.uncertainty: 0.10 arcsec centroid -> 0.15-0.64 kpc depending on cluster redshift
quantities.completeness: members above the catalogue magnitude limit
quantities.measurability_note: two independent astrometric solutions agree to 0.026 arcsec

quantities.name: y_compton
quantities.definition: Compton-y parameter: the line-of-sight integral of the electron pressure, from a calibrated SZ map.
quantities.source: MEASURED: a calibrated millimetre map
quantities.uncertainty: beam-convolved; correlated noise across the beam
exact_identities: y = (sigma_T / m_e c^2) integral P_e dl
quantities.measurability_note: RAW and independent of X-ray emissivity, which is exactly why it is worth having. An INTEGRATED Y_500 is NOT raw: its aperture is defined through a mass.

quantities.name: z
quantities.definition: Cartesian z-coordinate of the node in the cluster rest frame, origin at the declared centre. z is along the line of sight and is NOT measured.
quantities.source: sampled: only a scalar redshift is observed along the line of sight
